bandReport.notes: All five assigned pages (p02, p04, p06, p08, p10) opened and read; no page was empty. Items 1-23, continuous with no skips and no duplicates. Q1 opens p02 cleanly (it is the paper's first item) and Q23 ends p10 cleanly, so nothing runs across either band edge; item 24 belongs to the next band. COLUMN CROPS: all ten c1/c2 crops were clean - each opened on an item number and closed on a complete option block or the page footer, and no line was sliced. The c1 crops carry a narrow sliver of the neighbouring column's item numbers at their right edge (e.g. p02-c1 shows '4.' '5.' '6.'); that is cosmetic, costs no text, and independently corroborates which items sit in c2. p02 and p10 were additionally cross-read against the full-page renders and matched the column reading exactly. PRINTED INCONSISTENCIES, transcribed exactly as printed and NOT normalised: (i) Q11 option (d) is the bare '3', where the parallel options use the '1 only' / '2 only' form; (ii) Q16 option (d) is '2 and 4 only' while (a), (b) and (c) carry no 'only'; (iii) Q4 lists four statements but its code offers no option covering all four, the widest being '3 and 4'. None of these is an error on our side. SUBTOPIC OUTSIDE THE CATALOG: Q12 (empty seat in early Buddhist iconography) and Q14 (Amaravati Stupa relief sculpture) are both sculpture/iconography items. History > Art and Culture has Architecture, Literature, Painting and Music, Dance, and Theatre but no sculpture entry, and neither question is about architecture. Both are labelled 'Sculpture and Iconography' as a proposed catalog extension - subject and chapter are catalog-exact, so only a soft subtopic warning should result. TWO CLASSIFICATION CALLS worth a second eye, both defensible either way: Q7 (epigraphic place-value system, Mankani plates AD 595-596) is filed under Miscellaneous Historical Areas > Archaeology because it turns on inscriptional evidence, rather than under Ancient India > Gupta Empire and Post-Gupta Period; Q11 (Pleistocene river-course shift) is filed under Ancient India > Vedic Period because two of its three evidence options are textual/archaeological (Nadi-Sukta, Robert Bruce Foote), although its subject matter is Himalayan drainage and Geography > Indian Physical Geography: Rivers and Drainage would also fit. BLOCK BOUNDARY: items 1-20 are History/Art and Culture; the paper switches to Environment and Ecology at item 21. Per the brief, no answer field is supplied for any item.
